summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, and atrial fibrillation, was admitted for confusion, lethargy, and shortness of breath. He was found to have pneumonia in the left upper lobe, confirmed by chest CT, and was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioning to oral cefpodoxime and azithromycin. His altered mental status improved after bladder catheterization, which drained 2.5 liters of urine, and correction of hyponatremia and hypokalemia. He received a platelet transfusion and vitamin K for elevated INR due to recent anticoagulant changes. IVIG was administered to support immune function. He was restarted on lenalidomide prior to discharge and will follow up with hematology and cardiology. He was discharged home alert and ambulatory, with instructions to resume clean intermittent catheterization, stop smoking, and complete outpatient vaccinations.
